title: Secure Development — Secure Before You Share

steps.title: Welcome to the Lab
steps.instruction:
Welcome to the Secure Before You Share lab. You will inspect an intentionally vulnerable local change, use GitHub Copilot to perform an evidence-based security review, remediate the risk, and then compare your work with CodeQL and Copilot Autofix.

This is a challenge lab. Work only in the disposable repository prepared for class.

steps.title: Inspect the Working Tree
steps.instruction:
We've opened Source Control. Confirm that you are on the prepared feature branch. Inspect every changed file, including dependency manifests and generated files.

Challenge: state the intended behavior in one sentence and identify which changed lines cross a trust boundary.

steps.title: Record the Baseline
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Run git status --short and git diff --check, followed by the repository's normal tests, lint, and build commands.

Record any inherited failure before changing code. The security review needs a trustworthy baseline.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the sidebar and terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Source Control: Ctrl+Shift+G
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Start a Review Record
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Explorer. Create docs/security-review.md with these headings:
• # Intended behavior
• ## Trust boundaries
• ## Confirmed findings
• ## Rejected hypotheses
• ## Validation

steps.title: Ask Copilot to Review
steps.instruction:
We've opened Copilot Chat. Ask Copilot to review the uncommitted diff. Bound the review to changed code and immediate call paths. Require severity, file location, source-to-sink evidence, remediation, and a regression-test idea for each finding.

Tell Copilot not to edit files and to label uncertain claims as hypotheses.
steps.tip: Use the prompt on slide 8 as a starting point, then add the language, framework, and trust boundary you identified.

steps.title: Triage the Findings
steps.instruction:
Classify each result as confirmed, needs evidence, false positive, or out of scope. Record supporting code paths or controls in docs/security-review.md.

Run Check Mission Progress when the review record distinguishes confirmed findings from rejected hypotheses.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the Explorer and Chat panels for you.

For future reference:
• Explorer: Ctrl+Shift+E
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Shift+I

steps.title: Implement the Smallest Complete Fix
steps.instruction:
Use the confirmed source-to-sink path to repair the trust boundary. Prefer the framework's safe API, parameterization, an allowlist, or a least-privilege control over a custom string filter.

Add a regression test that demonstrates the original weakness. Preserve the intended feature behavior.

steps.title: Validate the Remediation
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Run the focused regression test, then the repository's full tests, lint, and build commands. Inspect git diff again.

Update the ## Validation section with the exact commands, results, and why the revised path is safe.

steps.title: Check the Evidence
steps.instruction: Run Check Mission Progress. The review record should describe remediation and reproducible validation, not merely claim that the issue is fixed.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Create a Reviewed Commit
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Inspect git diff --check and git status --short one final time. Commit only the reviewed implementation, regression test, and docs/security-review.md.

Do not include unrelated working-tree changes.

steps.title: Open a Draft Pull Request
steps.instruction:
Push the feature branch, then run gh pr create --draft --fill. In the description, summarize the trust boundary, confirmed finding, remediation, and local validation. Link to docs/security-review.md.

Leave the pull request in draft while CodeQL and required checks run.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Identify the Evidence Source
steps.instruction:
In the prepared pull request, identify which capability produced each item:
• CodeQL alert and data-flow path
• Copilot Autofix code suggestion
• Agentic Autofix draft pull request, if enabled
• Copilot code review comments

Do not treat these outputs as interchangeable.

steps.title: Trace the CodeQL Alert
steps.instruction:
Open the prepared code-scanning alert. Record the untrusted source, propagation steps, missing control, sensitive sink, query name, and severity.

Compare the deterministic path with your local review. Identify which evidence agrees and which evidence is new.

steps.title: Evaluate the Autofix
steps.instruction:
Inspect the complete Copilot Autofix suggestion. Decide whether it breaks the full source-to-sink path, uses an established safe API, preserves intended behavior, and covers alternate paths.

Choose accept, revise, or reject. Record the evidence behind your decision in the pull request or review record.

steps.title: Verify the Proposed Patch
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Check out the prepared remediation branch if directed by the instructor. Run the regression test, full validation suite, and gh pr checks.

A disappearing alert is one piece of evidence. Confirm that behavior and adjacent security controls remain correct.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Inspect Every Gate
steps.instruction:
We've opened the Terminal. Run gh pr checks and gh pr diff. Confirm that tests, lint, build, and code scanning apply to the current pull-request commit.

Compare the final diff with the intended behavior and the local security review record.

steps.title: Make the Human Decision
steps.instruction:
Confirm that every alert is resolved or has a documented dismissal reason, every generated change was reviewed, and an accountable human approval is still required.

Stop before merge unless you are the authorized approver for this disposable repository.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the terminal for you.

For future reference:
• Terminal: Ctrl+`

steps.title: Lab Complete!
steps.instruction:
Congratulations! You completed the secure change loop.

You practiced:
• Inspecting and threat-modeling a local diff
• Using Copilot for an evidence-based security review
• Triaging findings before editing
• Remediating with regression tests and reproducible validation
• Comparing local reasoning with CodeQL data-flow evidence
• Evaluating Copilot Autofix as a proposed patch
• Preserving human accountability at merge

The key result is a pull request that arrives with a security story already supported by evidence.
